description: The Office of Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur seeks a highly motivated Legislative Fellow to assist DC office in development and execution of policy and legislative strategy on a broad range of issues. Responsibilities of the Fellow will include contributions to hearings and conduct relevant research; to staff meetings and attend briefings; conduct research, prepare questions, and help draft materials for the Member, including legislation. This fellowship will come with a stipend and is for the remainder of 2019, with the possibility of extension into 2020. Women and minorities are encouraged to apply.

description: The House Judiciary Committee Democratic staff are looking for interns for the spring semester. The House Committee on the Judiciary's staff internship program offers undergraduate students, law students, graduate students, and recent graduates an opportunity to experience the operation of a congressional committee firsthand and learn about the important role that our Committee plays in the legislative process. The Judiciary Committee has jurisdiction over a wide range of legislative and oversight issues, including oversight of the U.S. Department of Justice, constitutional law, federal criminal law, voting rights, immigration and naturalization, intellectual property law, and antitrust law. The committee will be providing stipends to spring interns, with additional funds provided to interns with additional demonstrated financial need. The deadline to apply for the spring semester is October 1, 2019.
responsibilities: Researching policy issues under the committee's jurisdiction
Attending briefings and hearings on the Hill
Supporting committee clerks and professional staff members
Providing administrative support, including answering calls, delivering correspondence, and setting up the hearing room
qualifications: Undergraduate students, law students, graduate students, and recent graduates are eligible to apply
how_to_apply: To learn more and apply, visit https://judiciary.house.gov/internships. The deadline to apply for the spring semester is October 1, 2019.
equal_opportunity: The Committee does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including marital or parental status, sexual orientation, and gender identity), disability, age, or national origin.
